major.name: German Studies - BA

items.label: At least two outside the literature department

items.text: Further courses, including some offered by other departments, may be incorporated into the student's program if they bear directly on German studies (e.g. LTEU 110, LTEU 111, LTWL 160, LTWL 172, LTWL 176, LTWL 180, LTWL 183, MUS 113, PHIL 108, PHIL 183, TDHT 101, which frequently cover topics bearing on German studies; discuss in advance with the German studies adviser).
The five additional core courses must be "taken in at least two different departments."

items.label: Five additional core courses
items.notes: "Five additional core courses, taken in at least two different departments. At least two of these courses must be taken outside the literature department." Courses outside literature count toward the remaining three as well.

requirement.label: Twelve upper-division courses (forty-eight units) from the core course list

narrative: The required LTGM courses and other literature courses required for this major are not currently being offered, and the major is unavailable to declare from spring 2025 through the end of spring 2028. A minor is recommended.
The page says 'The major in German studies' without naming the degree; BA assumed.
The major in German studies requires twelve upper-division courses (forty-eight units) chosen from the core course list.
Students need to attain competence in German (two years of university-level language courses or the equivalent) before they can take certain required upper-division courses.
Students may petition to use up to five courses completed while studying abroad in their major.
In consultation with the program director and undergraduate adviser, students design individual plans of study from the many core courses.
GMST 196A/B (senior honors thesis; GPA of 3.5 in the major required) count among the required twelve for the major.

nodes.title: Reformation Europe
groups: The Major: Two courses in history
The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: The intellectual and social history of the Reformation and Counter-Reformation from the French invasions to the Edict of Nantes. Emphasis is upon reform from below and above, the transformation of grassroots spirituality into institutional control. +

nodes.title: Europe since 1945
groups: The Major: Two courses in history
The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: An analysis of European history since the end of the Second World War. Focus is on political, social, economic, and cultural developments within European societies as well as on Europe’s relationship with the wider world (the Cold War, decolonization).

nodes.title: The Spanish Civil War
groups: The Major: Two courses in history
The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: This course will examine the Spanish Civil War (1936–1939), from its long- and short-term causes, to the military conflict, the war’s internationalization, the violence perpetrated against civilians, the ideological stakes, the struggles of everyday life for the population, and the divided memory of the war that still inflames passions today. The course will view the war both through a Spanish lens and as a case study of broader trends including modern civil wars and the interwar European crisis.

nodes.title: European Intellectual History, 1780–1870
groups: The Major: Two courses in history
The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: European thought from the late Enlightenment and the French Revolution to Marx and Baudelaire, emphasizing the origins of romanticism, idealism, and positivism in England, Germany, and France.

nodes.title: European Intellectual History, 1870–1945
groups: The Major: Two courses in history
The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: A lecture-discussion course on the crisis of bourgeois culture, the redefinition of Marxist ideology, and the transformation of modern social theory. Readings will include Nietzsche, Sorel, Weber, Freud, and Musil. (This course satisfies the minor in the Humanities Program.)

nodes.title: The Holocaust as Public History
groups: The Major: Two courses in history
The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: We will study historical accounts, memoirs, diaries, and oral histories to master the Holocaust epoch. We will contrast scholarly narratives to personal experience as different ways to learn about the past. Students will design projects for public education.

nodes.title: Fascism, Communism, and the Crisis of Liberal Democracy: Europe 1919–1945
groups: The Major: Two courses in history
The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: A consideration of the political, social, and cultural crisis that faced Western liberal democracies in the interwar period, with emphasis on the mass movements that opposed bourgeois liberalism from both the left and the right.

nodes.title: Europe and the World I, 1808–1918
groups: The Major: Two courses in history
The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: A survey of Europe’s relationship to the world from the end of the Atlantic slave trade to the end of the first world war. Topics include Europe and slavery, colonialism, the global origins of the industrial revolution, explorers and knowledge transfer, nation-building and the American civil war, transnational social movements (abolitionism, feminism, socialism), global modernism, international trade, imperialism abroad and at home, colonial wars and genocides, World War I as a global conflict.

nodes.title: Europe and the World II, 1918–Present
groups: The Major: Two courses in history
The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: A survey of Europe’s relationship to the world from the end of World War I to the present. Topics include deglobalization, imperialism, and anti-imperialism; world economic crisis; global fascism; World War II as a global conflict; decolonization and neo-colonialism; the Cold War; racism and immigration; transnational social movements; popular culture and sports; human rights and global memory; the rise and the fall of communism; capitalism and environmentalism; the crisis of liberal democracy.

nodes.title: Modern German History: From Bismarck to Hitler
groups: The Major: Two courses in history
The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: An analysis of the volatile course of German history from unification to the collapse of the Nazi dictatorship. Focus is on domestic developments inside Germany as well as on their impact on European and global politics in the twentieth century.

nodes.title: Why Hitler? How Auschwitz?
groups: The Major: Two courses in history
The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: Why did Germany in 1919 produce an Adolf Hitler; how did the Nazis take power in 1933; and why did the Third Reich last until 1945? Why did the war against the Jews become industrial and absolute?

nodes.title: German Literature in Translation
groups: The Major: Three courses in German literature
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: One or more aspects of German literature, such as major authors, the contemporary novel, nineteenth-century poetry, German expressionism. Texts may be read in English or the original language. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Seminars in German Culture
groups: The Major: Three courses in German literature
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: (Cross-listed with LTGM 190.) These seminars are devoted to a variety of special topics, including the works of single authors, genre studies, problems in literary history, relations between literature and the history of ideas, literary criticism, literature and society, and the like. May be taken for credit up to two times as topics vary.

nodes.title: German Studies I: Aesthetic Cultures
groups: The Major: German Studies I and II
nodes.description: This course offers an overview of German aesthetic culture in its various forms (literature, film, art, music, and architecture) and methods of analysis. Materials will explore the diversity of aesthetic production from the eighteenth century to the present.

nodes.title: German Studies II: National Identities
groups: The Major: German Studies I and II
nodes.description: This course offers an overview of issues in contemporary and historical German cultures. How has national identity been constructed in the past? What does it mean to be a German in the new Europe? Materials include fiction, historical documents, films, and the internet.

nodes.title: German Literary Prose
groups: The Major: Three courses in German literature
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: The development of major forms and modes of German literary prose. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: German Poetry
groups: The Major: Three courses in German literature
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: The development of major forms and modes of German verse. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: New German Cinema
groups: The Major: Three courses in German literature
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: A survey of German cinema from the late 1960s to the early 1980s. Focus on films by such directors as Fassbinder, Herzog, Kluge, Schlӧndorff, von Trotta, and Wenders viewed in historical and cultural context. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Seminars in German Culture
groups: The Major: Three courses in German literature
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: (Cross-listed with LTEU 137.) These seminars are devoted to a variety of special topics, including the works of single authors, genre studies, problems in literary history, relations between literature and the history of ideas, literary criticism, literature and society, and the like. May be taken for credit up to two times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Philosophy and the Rise of Modern Science
The Rationalists
nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: The major writings of one or more of the seventeenth-century rationalists—Descartes, Spinoza, and Leibniz. Topics include the existence of God, the mind-body problem, free will, the nature of knowledge, belief, and error. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.

nodes.title: Topics in Early Modern Philosophy
nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: A study of one or more figures from seventeenth- and/or eighteenth-century philosophy, such as Bacon, Descartes, Hobbes, Cavendish, Conway, Spinoza, Locke, Malebranche, Leibniz, Astell, Berkeley, Du Chatelet, Hume, or Reid. The focus may be on particular texts or intellectual themes and traditions. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.

nodes.title: Kant
groups: The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.prereq_text: PHIL 32 or 33 or 104 or 105 or 111 or 112 or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: A study of selected portions of The Critique of Pure Reason and other theoretical writings and/or his major works in moral theory. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.

nodes.title: Hegel
groups: The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: A study of one or more of Hegel’s major works, in particular, The Phenomenology of Spirit and The Philosophy of Right. Readings and discussion may also include other figures in the Idealist tradition—such as Fichte, Hölderlin, and Schelling—and critics of the Idealist tradition—such as Marx and Kierkegaard. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.

nodes.title: History of Philosophy: Ancient
nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing and department stamp or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: An examination of ancient Greek philosophy, focusing on major works of Plato and Aristotle. PHIL 10, PHIL 111, and PHIL 112 should be taken in order.

nodes.title: History of Philosophy: Early Modern
nodes.prereq_text: PHIL 110, upper-division standing and department stamp or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: An examination of seventeenth- and eighteenth-century philosophy, focusing on major works of Descartes, Locke, and Hume. PHIL 110, PHIL 111, and PHIL 112 should be taken in order.

nodes.title: History of Philosophy: Late Modern
nodes.prereq_text: PHIL 111, upper-division standing and department stamp or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: An examination of late eighteenth and nineteenth-century philosophy, focusing on major works of Kant and Hegel. PHIL 110, PHIL 111, and PHIL 112 should be taken in order.

nodes.title: Phenomenology
groups: The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: An examination of the phenomenological tradition through the works of its major classical and/or contemporary representatives. Authors studied will vary and may include Brentano, Husserl, Heidegger, Stein, Merleau-Ponty, Levinas, and Irigaray. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.

nodes.title: Existentialism
groups: The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Classical texts and issues of existentialism. Authors studied will vary and may include Nietzsche, Kierkegaard, Heidegger, Sartre, de Beauvoir, and Fanon. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.

nodes.title: Revolution and Reaction: Political Thought from Kant to Nietzsche
groups: The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: The course deals with the period that marks the triumph and critique of the modern state. Central topics include the development of the idea of class, of the irrational, of the unconscious, and of rationalized authority as they affect politics. Readings drawn from Rousseau, Kant, Hegel, Marx, Nietzsche, and others.

nodes.title: Marxist Political Thought
groups: The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: An introduction to Marxist thought from its roots in the Western tradition through its development in non-Western contexts. Emphasis is placed on how adaptations were made in Marxism to accommodate the specific challenges of each environment.

nodes.title: The German Political System
groups: The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: An analysis of the political system of the Federal Republic of Germany with an emphasis on the party system, elections, executive-legislative relations, and federalism. Comparisons will be made with other West European democracies and the Weimar Republic.

nodes.title: Germany: Before, During, and After Division
groups: The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: Consideration of political, economic, and security factors that have kept Germany at the center of European developments for more than a century.

nodes.title: European Integration
groups: The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: This course reviews the origins and development of the European Community/European Union and its institutions, theories of integration and the challenges inherent in the creation of a supranational political regime.

nodes.title: The Holocaust
groups: The Major: At least two outside the literature department
The Major: Remaining additional core courses
nodes.description: The study of the unique and universal aspects of the Holocaust. Special attention will be paid to the nature of discrimination and racism, those aspects of modernity that make genocide possible, the relationship among the perpetrators, the victims and the bystanders, and the teaching, memory, and denial of the Holocaust.
